classification.difficultyReason: Derives a radius formula from tangent geometry and a half-angle, then evaluates it with specified rounding.

content.prompt: **Radius of the Moon.** Let $r$ denote the radius of the Moon, $\theta$ the angle subtended by the Moon when it is directly overhead, and $d$ the distance from the surface of the Moon to the surface of Earth.

spec.description: Earth surface at left; paired tangent sight lines to the Moon at right, with a dashed centre line and dashed tangent radii. Ordinary marks are black and the diagram is unshaded.
spec.mathematics: The sight-line angle is theta. The centre line bisects it and has length d+r. Each tangent radius has length r and meets its sight line at a right angle. Coordinates derive both tangent points from a common centre and radius; construction proportions are illustrative.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied labels and construction lines remain visible; no derived formula or numerical answer is drawn.

answer.worked:
The radius is perpendicular to the tangent sight line. The two right triangles are congruent, so the centre line bisects $\theta$.

$$\begin{align*}
\sin(\theta/2)&=\frac{r}{d+r}\\
(d+r)\sin(\theta/2)&=r\\
d\sin(\theta/2)+r\sin(\theta/2)&=r\\
r-r\sin(\theta/2)&=d\sin(\theta/2)\\
r\bigl(1-\sin(\theta/2)\bigr)&=d\sin(\theta/2)\\
r&=\frac{d\sin(\theta/2)}{1-\sin(\theta/2)}.
\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Given that $\theta=0.52^\circ$ and $d=384\,000$ kilometres, find $r$, to the nearest 10 kilometres.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
r&=\frac{384\,000\sin(0.52^\circ/2)}{1-\sin(0.52^\circ/2)}\\
r&=\frac{384\,000\sin 0.26^\circ}{1-\sin 0.26^\circ}\\
r&\approx1750.474117\text{ km}\\
r&\approx1750\text{ km}\quad\text{(nearest 10 km)}.
\end{align*}$$
